extracted.subtask_description: A print-news dispatch reporting wartime events, combining datelined foreign-bureau reports, translated official communiqués, battlefield descriptions, casualty counts, and human-interest anecdotes for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and attribute information to specific sources (e.g., 'United States Government monitors said', 'recorded and translated by the United States Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service', 'a spokesman said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article consistently ties claims to named sources or monitoring services rather than presenting unattributed assertions. Examples: 'Tokyo radio... recorded and translated by the United States Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service'; 'United States Government monitors said…'. Attribution helps readers assess credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish confirmed reports from unconfirmed or speculative accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly label reports that are unconfirmed or based on other broadcasts/rumors (e.g., 'There was no support...that Japanese broadcasts had been heard announcing the landing', 'it was believed', 'it was generally supposed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy avoids presenting uncertain items as facts; it flags absence of corroboration and frames some items as beliefs or suppositions. Anti-pattern: stating rumors as fact without noting lack of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primary recorded/translated material for foreign broadcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: When quoting foreign radio/official communiqués, rely on recorded translations and name the translating/monitoring body (e.g., 'recorded and translated by the United States Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the translation/monitoring authority increases reliability for readers and lets editors judge the chain of custody for quotes. Example: extensive quotation from a Tokyo broadcast with explicit recording/translation attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-source corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare reports from multiple outlets or monitoring services and note agreement or disagreement (e.g., Tokyo radio vs. Chungking radio; 'There was no support in this late broadcast from Chungking radio reports').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece highlights when different sources do or do not corroborate a claim, signaling to readers which items are better confirmed. Scoring note: stronger reporting shows corroboration across independent sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide operational and geographic detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific locations, dates/times, unit types, and operational descriptions (e.g., 'formation of carrier-based planes...raided our positions on the Truk Islands since yesterday morning', references to Anzio, Cassino, Staraya Russa, rail junctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed geographic and tactical reporting helps readers understand scope and significance. Example: datelined reports naming islands, towns, rail lines, and specific battle features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report significance and likely consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Add analysis of strategic or morale impact and possible follow-on effects (e.g., 'It was generally supposed that the event would have a profound effect on the morale of the Japanese people', 'Japan might now be compelled to withdraw some of her forces from China').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual interpretation (clearly labeled as such) helps readers grasp why events matter. Guidance: frame such analysis as opinion/belief when not directly attributable to authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight novel or unprecedented elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag unusual, first-time, or unprecedented developments reported by monitors (e.g., 'first time that they had heard on the Tokyo radio even an implied admission that possibly the Japanese navy was unequal to its task', 'an unprecedented exhortation for the production of “one more” warship').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noting novelty signals importance and historical value. Use direct quotes from sources when describing unprecedented statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify casualties, captures, and material effects with sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numbers for casualties, prisoners, losses, and material captures, and attribute them (e.g., 'More than 1,600 Germans were reported killed', 'captured 11,000 and the death of 52,000' as announced by Moscow/official communiqués).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric claims should be clearly attributed to their source and, where possible, contextualized. Avoid presenting conflicting figures without attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use human-interest and on-the-ground anecdotes to illustrate events
rubrics_metrics.description: Include soldier accounts, small-unit stories, and vivid scenes to humanize broader military developments (e.g., 'The story of how Cook’s detachment fought its way out of the trap', quoted dialogue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdotes enliven copy and convey lived experience; they should be clearly presented as individual accounts and, when possible, corroborated or contextualized by commanding statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use datelines and clear temporal markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin segments with datelines and include dates/times to place reports (e.g., 'Tokyo, February 18—', 'Chungking, Feb. 18 (4)—', 'Allied Headquarters, Naples, Feb. 18—(AP)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datelines and timestamps orient the reader geographically and chronologically and indicate wire-service sourcing. Maintain consistent formatting for datelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include visual aids or references to supporting maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference or provide maps and other visual information when covering complex geographic movements (e.g., the page notes 'Map on Page').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps and diagrams aid comprehension of multi-front operations; signal their presence in the text and ensure they align with reported locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report method and scale of military actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe forces and methods used (e.g., 'six-hour artillery barrage', '1,500 sorties', 'hundreds of guns', 'dive-bombed', 'tank-destroyers and bazookas'), conveying intensity and scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveying operational scale helps readers understand intensity; where available, pair with effects (casualties, breakthroughs, material damage). Avoid sensational hyperbole—use attributed figures and concrete descriptions.
